Matching cream to Bhopal's three seasons

Bhopal has a clear three-season year. Summers from April to June are hot and dry, the monsoon from about late June to September is humid and green around the lakes, and winters from November to February are cool and dry, with chilly nights in December and January. A simple way to rotate your stock:

  1. Summer: lighter textures. Avocado glow cream or a thin layer of avocado Korean night cream.
  2. Monsoon: keep it light. Avocado Korean night cream for most clients, avocado glow cream for oily skin.
  3. Winter: move to the richer avocado night cream, especially for clients who complain of tightness after washing.

Clients using any cream with kojic acid or glutathione should wear sunscreen the next morning. For the hot months, our night cream in summer guide is useful to share.

Wedding and festival rush

Parlours in Bhopal usually see their biggest demand around Navratri, Karwa Chauth, Diwali and the winter wedding season, with Eid bringing another busy spell. Pre-bridal packages and party facials are where bulk night cream gets used fastest. Order before the rush, so you are not waiting on a courier in your busiest week.

Storage tips for parlours

  • Store tubs sealed, out of direct sun and away from steamers and the wash area.
  • Scoop with a clean, dry spatula. Water or used tools in the tub are the most common cause of early spoilage.
  • Keep a small jar on the counter for the day and leave the main tub closed.
  • Write the date you opened each tub on the lid and use older tubs first.

Loose cream or ready jars?

Parlours and salons doing facials usually buy loose cream by the kilo. Cosmetic stores and resellers usually want finished jars. We do both. As a rough guide, 1 kg fills about 100 jars of 10 g, 66 jars of 15 g, 40 jars of 25 g or 33 jars of 30 g. Before buying in bulk, you can order one jar from the shop or request a sample.
